FOREW0R.D

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 10 June 1986, after the draft finalized by the Computers, Business Machines and Calculators Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard in three parts specifies the characteristics of 130 mm flexible disk cartridges recorded at 7 958 ftprad, 3.8 tpmm, on both sides using modified frequency modulation ( MFM ) recording. 0.3 Part 1 specifies the dimensional, physical and magnetic characteristics of the cartridge so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems. Together with the labelling scheme specified in IS : 11406-1986*/ IS0 7665-1983*, Part 1 and this part provide for full data interchange between data processing systems. Part 2 specifies an alternative track format for data interchange. 0.4 This standard is based on ISO/DIS 837813 Information processing Data interchange on 130 mm flexible disk cartridges using modified frequency modulation recording at 7 958 ftprad, 3.8 tpmm ( 96 tpi ), on two sides `Part 3 Track format B', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). _ 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 3 ) specifies the quality of recorded signals, the track layout, and a track format to be used on such a flexible disk cartridge, which is intended for data interchange between data processing systems.
*File structure and labelling of flexible disk cartridges for information interchange.

IS : 11853 ( Part 3 ) - 1986 3.4 Density of Recording 3.4.1 The nominal density of recording nominal bit cell length is 125.5 prad. shall be 7 958 ftprad. The

3.4.2 The long-term average bit cell length shall be the average bit cell length measured ov,er a sector. It shall be within f 3.5 percent of the nominal bit cell length. 3.4.3 The short-term average bit cell length, referred to a particular bit cell, shall be the average of the lengths of the preceding eight bit cells. It shall be within & 8 percent of the long-term average bit cell length. 3.5 Flus Transition Spacing ( seeFig. 2 )

The instantaneous spacing between flux transitions may be influenced by the reading and writing process, the bit sequence recorded ( pulse The locations of the transitions crowding effects ), and other factors. are defined as the locations of the peaks in the signal when reading. Tests should be carried out using a peak-sensing amplifier. 3.5.1 The spacing between the flux transitions in a sequence of ONE's shall be between 80 and 120 percent of the short-term average bit cell length. 3.5.2 The spacing between the flux transition for a ONE and that between two ZERO's preceding or following it shall be between 130 and 165 percent of the short-term average bit cell length. 3.5.3 The spacing between the two ONE flux transitions surrounding a ZERO bit cell shall lie between 185 and 225 percent of the short-term average bit cell length. ?

A byte is a group of eight bit-positions, identified Bl to B8, with B8 the most significant and recorded first. The bit in each position is a ZERO or a ONE. 3.8 Sector 3.9 Track .

APPENDIX ( Clause 3.1.3 )
EDC IMPLEMENTATION A-O. Figure 6 shows the feedback connections may be used to generate the EDC bytes.

A

of a shift register which

A-L Prior to the operation, all positions of the shift register are set to ONE. Input data are added ( exclusive OR ) to the contents of position Cl, of the register to form a feedback. This feedback is in its turn added ( exclusive OR ) to the contents of position Cl4 and C11. A-2. On shifting, the outputs of the exclusive OR gates are entered aespectively into positions Co, C, and C12. After the last data bit has been added, the register is shifted once more as specified above. The register then contains the EDC bytes. 12

IS : 11853 ( Part A-3. If further shifting is to take place during the writing bytes, the control signal inhibits exclusive OR operations.

3 ) - 1986

of the EDC

A-4. To check for errors when reading, the data bits are added into the shift register in exactly the same manner as they were during writing. After the data, the EDC bytes are also entered into the shift register as After the final shift, the register contents will be all if they were data. ZERO if the record does r&t contain errors.

APPENDIX ( Clause 6.1 )

B

PROCEDURE AND EQUlPMENT FOR MEASURING FLUX TRANSITION SPACING B-l. GENERAL

This appendix specifies an equipment and a procedure for measuring flux transition spacing on 130 mm flexible disk cartridges using MFM recording at 7 958 ftprad on two sides. B-2. FORMAT The disk to be measured shall be written by the disk drive for data interchange use. Testing shall be done on tracks 00 and 79 on both sides. The test patterns 11011011 (DB) and 11011100 (DC) shall be written repeatedly on each test track. B-3. TEST B-3.1 EQUIPMENT

Disk Drive

The disk drive shall have a rotational speed of 300 rev/min, with a tolerance of + 3 rev/min, averaged over one revolution. 13

IS : 11853 ( Part 3 ) - 1986 The average angular speed taken over 64 ps shall not deviate by more than 0'5 percent from the speed averaged over one revolution. B-3.2 Head

B-3.2.1 Resolution - The head shall have an absolute resolution of 55 to 65 percent at track 79 on each side, applying the calibration factor of the reference material appropriate to the side, and recording with the appropriate test recording current. The resonant frequency of the head shall be at least 250 000 Hz. The resolution shall not be adjusted by varying the load impedance to. the head. The resolution defined in B-3.3.1. shall be measured at the output of the amplifier 6

B-3.2.2 O&ret Angle - The head shall have a gap offset angle of 0" f with the disk radius on the testing drive. B-3.2.3 Contact - Care shall be taken contact with the media during the tests. B-3.3 Read Channel that the heads are in good

B-3.3.1 Read Amplzjier - The read amplifier shall have a flat response from 1 000 to 187 500 Hz within &- 1 dB, and amplitude saturation shall not occur. B-3.3.2 Peak Sensing Am@lif;er - Peak sensing shall be carried a differentiating and limiting amplifier.

APPENDIX ( Clause 6.2 )
DATA SEPARATORS recording FOR DECODING method gives C-l. The MFM spacings of:

C
. MFM nominal RECORDING flux transition

t for the patterns 1 1 or 0 0 0 3t/2 for the patterns 1 0 or 0 1 22 for the pattern 1 0 1 C-2. The data separator shall be capable of resolving a difference of only 2 ps. To achieve this with a low error rate, the separator cannot operate on a fixed period but shall follow changes in the bit cell length. C-3. It is recognized that various techniques may be developed to achieve dynamic data separation; with present technology only an analogue data separator based on a phase-locked Ioscillator can provide the necessary reliability.
